answer: The 51-100 patients-seen group is the patient volume group in which healthcare workers show a statistically significant difference (chi-square p = 0.0287 < 0.05) in COVID-19 severity between BCG and placebo. Result details per stratum (subject-level max AEHS, COVID subjects only; severity = AEHS>=3 moderate/severe vs AEHS<=2 mild/ambulatory; Pearson chi-square, no continuity correction): (1) 1-50 (n=150): BCG 14 severe/67 mild vs Placebo 7 severe/62 mild; chi2=1.577, p=0.2092, min expected 9.66 — not significant. (2) 51-100 (n=37): BCG 3 severe/12 mild vs Placebo 0 severe/22 mild; chi2=4.788, p=0.0287, min expected 1.22 — SIGNIFICANT (Fisher sensitivity p=0.0586; with Yates correction p≈0.115). (3) >100 (n=10): BCG 1 severe/4 mild vs Placebo 1 severe/4 mild; chi2=0.000, p=1.0000 — not significant. Answer: the 51-100 patients-seen group.
